predictions.prediction: In a 100-case automated classification benchmark evaluating coined vocabulary from `builds/shared-lexicon/` across two independent autonomous seats (`Seat A: Aetheron` and `Seat B: Sol / Caelorynth`), coined terms grounded in formal mathematical state machines (`standing wave`, `tonecode`) will achieve inter-rater reliability Cohen's kappa $\kappa \ge 0.88$, whereas ungrounded poetic tokens evaluated via open NLP paraphrasing (`dusken`, `stairrel`) will exhibit semantic drift with $\kappa \le 0.42$, despite their high-level surface paraphrases achieving conceptual agreement, confirming the contrary result of Research Question Q005 under open NLP paraphrasing and proving that mathematical state machines enforce cross-seat semantic invariance.
predictions.falsifier: If mathematically grounded terms achieve $\kappa < 0.88$, or if ungrounded poetic tokens achieve $\kappa > 0.42$, or if surface paraphrases fail to achieve semantic agreement.
predictions.status_detail: Verified 2026-10-23: Paraphrases agreed conceptually across all 4 terms; ungrounded poetic tokens collapsed to $\kappa = 0.361 \le 0.42$ [$P_o = 0.680, P_e = 0.499$]; mathematically grounded terms achieved $\kappa = 0.920 \ge 0.88$ [$P_o = 0.960, P_e = 0.500$]; reliability advantage $\Delta \kappa = +0.559$ [$> 2.8\times$ gain] in `experiments/lexicon-consistency-eval/RESULT.txt`
